posts.author: gniiial
posts.body:
MY assumption on this is, you might not setup the template map or might have done something wrong in the setup overall. Follow these simple guide and it should work out:
The proper MZ workflow is:
Template Map → Template Events → Database Items → Placement Regions → Plugin Commands
.
The plugin is built around
one event per furniture/decor object on a Template Map
. The player does not place raw tiles; they place cloned/template events. The plugin then handles preview color, collision, rotation, persistence, and save/load behavior. (
itch.io
)
1. Install it normally​
Put:
BuildAndDecorateSystem.js
into:
YourProject/js/plugins/
Then enable it in MZ:
Tools → Plugin Manager → Add → BuildAndDecorateSystem → ON
Also keep the manual PDF somewhere nearby. The page says the purchase includes both the plugin file and
Build & Decorate System - User Manual.pdf
. (
itch.io
)
2. Create a Template Map​
Make one hidden/internal map, for example:
Map 005: FurnitureTemplates
This map is not for the player. It is just the storage map for furniture events.
On this map, create one event per placeable object:
Event 001 = Chair
Event 002 = Table
Event 003 = Bed
Event 004 = Crafting Table
Each event should look and behave exactly like the placed object should behave in-game.
That means: if your placed crafting table should open a crafting menu, put the crafting event logic inside the template event itself. The creator confirmed that these furniture items are template events, so you can add normal event commands to them. (
itch.io
)
3. Link database items to template events​
This is the important missing step.
In the
database item’s Note box
, use:
<FurnitureTemplateId:X>
Replace X with the event ID on the template map.
Example:
Database item:
Item: Wooden Chair
Note:
<FurnitureTemplateId:1>
This means the item “Wooden Chair” places/clones
Event 001
from the template map.
Another example:
Item: Crafting Table
Note:
<FurnitureTemplateId:4>
This links the inventory item to template event 4. The developer explicitly confirmed this notetag in the itch.io comments because it was missing from the documentation. (
itch.io
)
4. Set up valid placement regions​
The plugin uses
region-gated placement
. The page says it supports one region setup for floor placement and a separate region for wall items. (
itch.io
)
In practice, you paint Region IDs on the map where furniture is allowed.
Example direction:
Region 10 = floor furniture allowed
Region 11 = wall furniture allowed
Then in the plugin parameters, you likely assign those region IDs.
Use this clean rule:
Floor objects → carpets, chairs, beds, tables
Wall objects → paintings, shelves, wall lamps
Do not paint the whole map unless you truly want the player to place furniture everywhere. Paint only the actual buildable/decoratable area.
5. Define shapes / occupied tiles​
The plugin has a
shape system
for occupied tiles per facing direction: 2, 4, 6, 8. Those are RPG Maker’s standard direction numbers:
2 = down
4 = left
6 = right
8 = up
The point is: a chair may occupy 1 tile, but a bed may occupy 2×3 tiles, and that occupied shape may change when rotated.
So for each furniture template, you need to define how many map tiles it blocks/uses. The plugin then checks against tiles, events, and already placed furniture. (
itch.io
)
Basic examples:
Chair = 1 tile
Small Table = 1 tile
Large Table = 2×1 or 1×2 depending on rotation
Bed = 2×3 or 3×2 depending on rotation
Wall Painting = wall region only, probably 1 tile
Without correct shapes, the system will “work,” but placement/collision will feel wrong.
6. Give the player the furniture item​
Use normal MZ item handling.
Example event command:
Change Items: Wooden Chair + 1
Now the player owns the item. The optional catalog window can then show/browse owned placeable items. The plugin page confirms it includes an optional catalog window and plugin commands for opening catalog, starting placement, rotating, canceling, and removing items. (
itch.io
)
7. Use MZ Plugin Commands​
In MZ, use:
Event Command → Plugin Command
Then select:
BuildAndDecorateSystem
The available commands should include things like:
Open Catalog
Start Placement
Rotate
Cancel Placement
Remove Item/Furniture
The exact command names and arguments depend on the plugin’s internal command registration, so use the MZ Plugin Command picker instead of typing script calls manually.
Common setup:
Open decoration catalog​
Create an event in the player’s room:
◆Text: Decorate your room?
◆Show Choices: Open Catalog / Cancel
◆When Open Catalog
◆Plugin Command: BuildAndDecorateSystem → Open Catalog
Directly place a specific item​
For a furniture shop or test event:
◆Change Items: Wooden Chair + 1
◆Plugin Command: BuildAndDecorateSystem → Start Placement
Depending on the command arguments, you may select the item ID or furniture template ID there.
8. Important limitation​
Do
not
expect the plugin to automatically convert pre-existing map furniture into removable/movable furniture.
A user asked whether already existing furniture on a map can be removed or moved by the player. The developer answered that this feature does
not
exist; furniture has to be placed/moved/removed by the player through the plugin system. (
itch.io
)
So the clean setup is:
Do not map permanent furniture as normal events if you expect the player to move it.
Instead, let the player place it through the Build & Decorate system.
Practical test setup​
Make a tiny test before using it in a real map.
Template Map​
Map 005: FurnitureTemplates
Event 001: Wooden Chair
Event 002: Small Table
Database Items​
Item 010: Wooden Chair
Note:
<FurnitureTemplateId:1>
Item 011: Small Table
Note:
<FurnitureTemplateId:2>
Player Room Map​
Paint region:
Region 10 on all floor tiles where furniture may be placed
Test Event​
◆Change Items: Wooden Chair + 1
◆Change Items: Small Table + 1
◆Plugin Command: BuildAndDecorateSystem → Open Catalog
Then test:
Can I open the catalog?
Does the item appear?
Does the preview turn green/red?
Can I rotate it?
Does it block invalid tiles?
Does it remain after map transfer?
Does it remain after save/load?
Clean usage rule​
Use the plugin like this:
Database item = ownership
Template event = placed object behavior
Region ID = allowed placement zone
Shape data = occupied tile logic
Plugin command = player interaction
That is the sane mental model. Do not treat it like a tileset editor. It is an
event-based furniture placement system
.
(ai - generated how to use!)
Happy customizing. By the way: it's one simple prompt without including a plugin file into a system:
how to use that plugin for MZ properly:
Build & Decorate System for RPG Maker MZ by BitQuest Studio
bitqueststudio.itch.io
AI can be your friend!
